rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The biofield as a working language", "body": "Chance said he did not know whether the biofield was a literal structure of nature, and suggested the whole idea could be imaginary yet still work as if it were real. He described it as a language that gave practitioners an intellectual scaffolding for understanding the messages the body sends. Chance compared it to naming, noting that a deer is not called a deer by nature, and said he believed language could still describe truth. He credited Eileen Day McKusick's book Tuning the Human Biofield as the source of the map he learned from."}, {"title": "Remote sessions and the idea of distance", "body": "Chance said most of his sessions were remote, because the people he worked with lived far away and he had no studio space. He described setting up a stand-in body on a table with crystals and candles so he could measure distances from it. Asked how remote and in-person work compared, Chance said he used Zoom so a session could be recorded, and began with a spoken agreement about intentions and which beings were welcome. He added that remote work gave people experiential knowledge that separation is a mental concept."}, {"title": "Forks, Solfeggio tones, and number patterns", "body": "Chance said he favored the Solfeggio range while maintaining that any coherent vibration could help the body self-correct. He distanced himself from online videos claiming specific frequencies repair DNA, saying he had never seen an origin for those charts. He described liking a low 174 weighted fork for hearing pitch changes, and a large 384 fork as his first pick if he could only use one. Chance also walked through digit reductions and differences in the Solfeggio set that kept returning to three, six, and nine, which he read as a Trinity pattern and called his own opinion."}, {"title": "Old beliefs as forgotten device settings", "body": "Chance compared forgotten beliefs to settings chosen on a new device and never revisited. He described a belief absorbed in childhood as something that could keep a small share of personal energy tied up, and said that bringing it back to conscious attention could return that energy to circulation. He also said the effects of a tuning could keep unpacking in the body for about three days. Chance offered his view that finishing small tasks and tidying a living space reflected how much personal energy a person had available."}, {"title": "Valuing yourself as an independent healer", "body": "Chance told aspiring healers that offering value required valuing their own time. He said the sacral center related to self worth, and that the price a healer asked should cover what was needed to stay in a good working state, not an hourly figure. He argued that a real investment might help recipients value the change. Chance also said that making it up as you go felt like being in the zone, provided the intention was honest."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I returned to Ascension of the Chessmen with Andre Mitty for an incredible flow state about sound, energy balancing healing modalities, and the mindset required to value yourself as an independent aura technician. https://www.spreaker.com/user/12156556/chancegarton
